thread.title: Intel To Gain All iPhone Share, as Qualcomm, Broadcom Lose, Says Instinet - Barron's

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Intel To Gain All iPhone Share, as Qualcomm, Broadcom Lose, Says Instinet - Barron's
text:
Instinet ’s Romit Shah this morning writes that Apple ’s ( AAPL ) report last week of sales of 77.3 million iPhones in the December quarter was “decently below the Apple’s original expectations,” and so as a result, the company’s going to choose cheaper parts for some or all of the new models it puts out this year.
“Many consumers are simply not yet willing to pay $1,200 for a phone,” he muses.
That may hurt Qualcomm ( QCOM ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ), writes Shah, while benefitting Intel ( INTC ) and Qorvo ( QRVO ), as they take share from the other two.
Broadcom has been pursuing a hostile bid for Qualcomm since November, and this morning raised its bid for the latter .
Shah reiterates the same basic rumors about this year’s new iPhones , suggesting there’ll be one that uses a conventional LCD screen, measuring 6.1 inches on the diagonal, with a “near bezel-less” screen and costing just $700 to $900, versus the $1,00 iPhone. Two OLED models will also be offered.
He cites data from Taiwanese colleagues suggesting Apple is planning the LCD model to be the biggest seller of the three:
Our research colleagues in Taiwan recently indicated that Apple is adding more suppliers for the 6.1” LCD iPhone (“Quantifying the impact of iPhone order cuts”). This includes Hon Hai in EMS (in addition to Pegatron and Wistron), LGD in display (besides JDI), Jabil in metal frame casing (besides Catcher and Casetek) and more new antenna suppliers (including Flexium). In addition, we believe that Apple is reducing the iPhone BOM in an effort to preserve profits.
One conclusion about the chips is Intel ’s modems are now good enough to replace Qualcomm across the board:
We believe Apple will also source 100% of thin modems from Intel; another example of ‘good enough’. Intel is currently sampling its XMM7560 modem, which introduces CDMA technology for the first time and supports speeds up to 1.6GB per second. Intel has been developing CDMA & 5G-functionality for a number of years, and now the capabilities of these technologies appear to have matured to Apple’s specifications. Intel plans to introduce the full 5G capable XMM 8000 series modem in late 2020. For comparison, all Qualcomm modems support CDMA and have featured Gigabit LTE for multiple generations (X16 & X20), while the upcoming X50 modem will support full 5G and launches in 1H19. • Qualcomm’s modem technology is solid, but Intel modems cost less while still meeting Apple’s standards. Assuming typical yoy ASP increases, we believe that moving to 100% Intel modems could save Apple roughly $105mn cycle-over-cycle, as seen in Fig. 6. We estimate the gross margin on Intel’s iPhone modem in the low 30% range, whereas we estimate Qualcomm’s iPhone margins at approx. 40%, at the low- end of QCT margins. Using Intel modems across all iPhone SKUs also provides Apple with leverage against Qualcomm during the ongoing licensing dispute between the two companies. Impact to CY20E Revenue & EPS.
Broadcom is also at risk: It’s going to lose the “ PAD ” filter socket in the LCD version to Qorvo, he thinks, something he sees confirmed by last week’s Qorvo earnings call.
"Broadcom’s iPhone content will decline for the first time; from a blended average of $23 in the iPhone X / 8 to $19 in the 2018 next-gen phones."
Historically, Apple has used Broadcom’s latest bulk acoustic wave (BAW) technology to enable high-band cellular filtering. BAW is the primary solution for enabling cellular filtering above 1.5GHz. There are two methods of performing BAW filtering; one leverages the film bulk acoustic resonance (FBAR) technology that Broadcom absorbed from Avago, while the other is ‘solid mounted resonator’ or BAW-SMR technology that Triquint brought to the 2014 RFMD merger (which created Qorvo). The primary difference between the two technologies is how acoustic energy is trapped and how heat is dispersed. Qorvo has encountered challenges developing its BAW-SMR technology, at one point battling sub-optimal yields, but it is apparent that the current solution meets Apple’s standards. Qorvo’s win represents approximately $100mn in BOM cost savings for Apple and a roughly $400mn revenue headwind for Broadcom in 2H18.
One other conclusion, is it would be “good” for Broadcom to succeed in buying Qualcomm . Among other things, "If Broadcom acquires Qualcomm, we estimate combined company EBITDA would grow from $21 billion in CY17E to approximately $28bn in CY20E,” writes Shah.
Qualcomm stock is down $1.50, or 2%, at $64.57, Broadcom stock is up $5.22, or 2%, at $240.70, Intel shares are up 41 cents, or 0.8%,a t $46.56, and Qorvo is up 5 cents at $80.82.
